pulse: The roof is done and the cabin warm, but tomorrow's fuel run looms with winter pressing in—the family plans together, tired but steady, ready for the next build.
scene: Evening is cooling and clear; the family gathers warm at the cabin with hot dinner, Cole planning tomorrow's fuel run while Finn chatters about the woodshed and Maggie settles them all with care.

day_summaries.1: Day one: Finn's instinct proved right, the spring flows clear on the ridge, and the family's first night settles warm with hot soup and plans. Water changes everything—Cole's already sketching the pipeline for tomorrow. They're exactly where they meant to be.
day_summaries.2: Day two brought focus: Cole and Sawyer completed the spring intake while the family cleared willows and tended the cabin. Food stores are now empty—but tomorrow Finn fishes, and tonight they rest warm and whole. Foundation work waits next, and their quiet confidence in the land grows each day.
day_summaries.3: Day 3 brought the family's first salmon—Finn caught them with pride; Cole's water system came online, spring flowing clean. Exhausted but settling in, they know they're not just surviving now. Finn is sick and drained, but the day drew them closer; tonight they rest whole.
day_summaries.4: Day 4 broke: Cole, Sawyer, Finn, and Bear fished the creek and landed salmon—their first real meal. As evening settles, the family gathers warm by the stove, fed and hopeful, the strain easing. Tomorrow Cole will push the roof patch while weather holds.
day_summaries.5: Day 5 brought the first real catch—three fish pulled from the creek, Sawyer teaching with patience he didn't know he had, Finn proud of his own hook, and Bear gleeful in the work. With real food in their bellies and the cabin warm, the family faces nightfall stronger than in days.
day_summaries.6: Day 6's patching moved the cabin to 71%—Cole, Sawyer, and injured Finn pushing hard in endless light, while Maggie readied tomorrow's crucial town run. The family is exhausted and hungry but held by genuine progress. Sawyer felt his father's real trust for the first time, and something changed.
day_summaries.7: Day seven brought the Wilders their first real harvest: Sawyer taught the boys to fish and they caught enough for a full meal. The cabin glows warm now, exhaustion mixing with satisfaction as Maggie tends sick Bear and the others rest. For the first time in days, the family breathes easier.
day_summaries.8: Day 8: Cole and Sawyer locked in roof beams while Finn hauled and Maggie made thin dinner at the porch—the family running on fumes but warm, and one day from the shelter that'll carry them through winter. Tired, hungry, and still believing.
day_summaries.9: The family raced the roof to completion in a single daylong push, sealing the cabin against weather just as summer's endless light began to fade. Cole, Sawyer, and Finn pushed through coughs while Maggie kept them fed and warm; Bear ran scraps with fierce pride. By nightfall the roof was done, the stove glowed, and though three boys were sick and the pantry was thin, the family was home—safe, together, and ready for what winter would demand.
day_summaries.10: Day 10: the roof held through daylong work, and the family moved through wood reorganization with earned confidence. Sawyer stepped into real build responsibility and earned Cole's affirmation; the younger boys pushed through the work with growing strength. By nightfall, they gathered at the fire, warm and closer—one more week like this locks in winter-readiness.
day_summaries.11: Day 11 brought the family their first real rest—the roof now secure and Finn catching his first fish at the creek. By evening they gathered on the porch as the aurora danced, tired but whole and looking forward to winter with newfound confidence.

lean.label: Push the roof
lean.desc: Trust the momentum and the clear skies; winter's waiting
